title: A heartbeat you can hear
body: By now the heart is beating steadily — about twice as fast as yours — and strong enough to find on a doppler at your next visit.

title: The size of a secret
body: Your baby is measured crown-to-rump this trimester, like measuring a tiny curled-up secret.

title: Taste buds in training
body: Flavours from what you eat drift into the amniotic fluid. Dinner tonight is, in a small way, a shared meal.

title: Tiny fingerprints
body: The ridges that will become fingerprints are forming — a signature no one else on earth will ever have.

title: Practising breath
body: Long before the first cry, your baby rehearses breathing motions with the amniotic fluid. Rehearsal for the big debut.

title: Hiccups happen
body: Those small rhythmic jumps you may feel soon? Practice-breathing hiccups. Completely normal, quietly adorable.

title: Growing ears
body: The ears are migrating to their final spots and the inner ear is wiring up. Your voice is becoming their first music.

title: A leap every week
body: Each week of pregnancy brings something new that wasn't there seven days ago — that's the quiet magic of the Journey tab.

title: The nesting instinct is real
body: Late pregnancy brings a documented urge to prepare the home. Biologists call it nesting; you call it a Saturday well spent.

title: Kicks get stronger
body: What starts as bubbles and flutters becomes unmistakable rolls and thumps — usually felt first between weeks 18 and 25.

title: Baby's sleep cycles
body: By the third trimester your baby has real sleep-wake cycles — and, maddeningly, often wakes when you lie down.

title: Vernix, the original lotion
body: A creamy protective coat called vernix covers your baby's skin in the final weeks — nature's first moisturiser.

title: Water before coffee
body: A tall glass of water first thing eases nausea, headaches, and the third-trimester puffiness. Your future self says thanks.

title: Small meals, often
body: Five little meals sit better than three big ones right now — steadier energy, calmer stomach.

title: The left-side trick
body: Sleeping on your left side improves blood flow to the placenta. A pillow between the knees makes it genuinely comfortable.

title: Write one sentence
body: Future-you will treasure even a single honest sentence about today. It doesn't have to be profound to be precious.

title: Photograph the bump today
body: It changes faster than you think. A quick photo in the same spot each week becomes the most-watched slideshow of your life.

title: Rest is productive
body: Growing a human is metabolic hard labour. A nap is not laziness; it is, quite literally, the work.

title: Say the strange symptom out loud
body: Nothing is too weird to mention to your provider. They've heard it all, and asking beats wondering at 3am.

title: Snack before you rise
body: A plain cracker on the nightstand, eaten before you sit up, is the oldest morning-sickness trick because it works.

title: Moisturise the bump
body: A slow minute with oil or lotion on the belly is part skincare, part first conversation with the baby.

title: Gentle movement counts
body: A ten-minute walk after dinner settles digestion, sleep, and mood. No gear, no goals, just motion.

title: Keep a questions note
body: Between appointments, park every question in one place. Bring the list; leave with answers instead of 'oh, I forgot to ask'.

title: Take a chore without being asked
body: Pick one recurring task and silently make it yours for the rest of the pregnancy. It lands better than any gift.

title: Learn this week's size
body: Knowing whether the baby is a fig or a grapefruit this week makes you a real participant, not a spectator.

title: Ask about the feeling, not just the fact
body: 'How are you feeling about it all?' opens a door that 'how are you?' keeps closed.

title: Run the craving errand gladly
body: The midnight pickle run is pregnancy folklore for a reason. Do it with ceremony and you're a legend.

title: Book the thing
body: Research one appointment, class, or purchase end-to-end so she never has to chase it. Ownership is the love language of trimester two.

title: Write to the baby
body: A note to the little one — your voice, your hopes — becomes a keepsake they'll read at eighteen.

title: Feet up, phone down
body: Ten undivided minutes each evening — no screens — is worth more than an hour of half-attention.

title: Pack your own bag too
body: The hospital bag isn't just hers. Snacks, charger, a change of clothes, and the camera are your department.

title: Brag about her to the baby
body: Tell the bump, out loud, how amazing its mother is. She'll pretend it's silly. It isn't.

title: Guard the calendar
body: Protect her rest like it's a meeting with the boss. Because it is — and you're the gatekeeper.

title: One photo, today
body: Take one photo of this ordinary day — the bump, the couch, the two of you. Ordinary now, treasure later.

title: Name the feeling
body: Each say one word for how today felt. No fixing, no advice — just say it and hear it.

title: Plan the announcement photo
body: If you haven't told everyone yet, dream up how you'll do it. Half the fun is the scheming.

title: A ten-minute dream session
body: What do you want the first week home to look like? Ten minutes of dreaming together is real preparation.

title: Start the hospital list
body: Even months early, a running list lowers the background hum of 'are we ready?'.

title: Cook one craving kindly
body: Pick tonight's dinner from the craving list, made the gentle way.

title: Record the heartbeat
body: At your next appointment, ask to record the heartbeat on a phone. It's the first voice memo that matters.

title: Choose the first outfit
body: One tiny outfit, chosen together, makes the whole thing wonderfully real.

title: Walk and talk
body: A short evening walk, phones away, one question each: what are you most excited for?

title: Write this week's headline
body: If this week of your pregnancy were a newspaper, what's the headline? Save it in the journal.

title: The bump has a soundtrack
body: Your baby hears the world muffled, like underwater — but your voice comes through clearest of all.

title: Hair, maybe
body: Some babies arrive bald as a pebble, others with a full head of hair. Heartburn folklore aside, it's a genetic lottery.

title: A full grip
body: By late pregnancy your baby can grasp — that iron-strong newborn grip is being rehearsed right now.

title: The due date is a guess
body: Only about 1 in 20 babies arrive on their due date. Think of it as a season, not a deadline.

title: Placenta: the temporary organ
body: Your body grew an entirely new organ for this project, and will retire it gracefully when the work is done.

title: Dreams get vivid
body: Pregnancy hormones turn up the volume on dreams. Bizarre is normal; write the good ones down.

title: Baby's first cells know the plan
body: From a single cell, every instruction for every freckle is already written. The whole story is underway.

title: Your blood volume is up ~50%
body: Your heart is pumping for two, moving almost half again as much blood as before pregnancy.

title: Protein at breakfast
body: Eggs, yogurt, or nut butter in the morning steadies blood sugar and tames the mid-morning quease.

title: Compression socks are chic now
body: If ankles are swelling by evening, gentle compression socks in the morning genuinely help.

title: Stretch before bed
body: Slow calf and hip stretches before sleep cut down the 2am leg-cramp ambush.

title: Let people help
body: When someone offers, say yes and name a task. Help given is love accepted.

title: One prenatal class, booked
body: You don't need every class. One good one, booked early, beats five you'll rush to later.

title: Read one week ahead
body: Skim next week's changes so nothing she mentions surprises you. Prepared is attractive.

title: Handle the admin
body: Insurance, leave paperwork, the registry logistics — unglamorous, unforgettable.

title: Learn the nap schedule
body: Hers, not the baby's. Defend it like a dragon guards gold.

title: Touch the bump with permission
body: Ask, then linger. Feeling a kick for the first time rearranges something in a person.

title: The name shortlist
body: Each bring three names to the couch tonight. Vetoes allowed, mockery banned.

title: One screen-free evening
body: Tonight: cook, talk, maybe fold something tiny. The apps will survive without you both.

title: Photograph the nursery corner
body: Even if it's still a closet full of boxes. 'Before' photos make the 'after' sing.

title: Say it to the mirror
body: 'I'm doing something extraordinary.' Daily. Cheesy, and also true.

title: The first kicks feel like popcorn
body: Most describe quickening as popcorn popping or a fish turning over — subtle, then suddenly obvious.

title: Colostrum arrives early
body: Your body may start making the first milk weeks before birth. The kitchen opens before the guests arrive.

title: Pick the paediatrician
body: A short list and one meet-and-greet now saves a scramble later.
